claims.text: OpenTelemetry is an open standard with libraries for producing telemetry: an API that code calls, an SDK that collects and exports, and OTLP, the protocol for sending the data on. It does not store or display traces; that is left to other tools such as Tempo and Grafana.
claims.source_hint: OpenTelemetry docs 'What is OpenTelemetry?' (not an observability backend) and 'Specification overview' (API, SDK, OTLP)

claims.text: In .NET a span is represented by System.Diagnostics.Activity, started from an ActivitySource; these .NET types are the implementation of OpenTelemetry's tracing API (Tracer, Span), so libraries call them rather than an OpenTelemetry package.
claims.source_hint: OpenTelemetry .NET docs 'Instrumentation' / 'Traces' (Activity = span, ActivitySource = tracer); .NET docs 'Distributed tracing instrumentation'

claims.text: The OpenTelemetry .NET SDK records only activities from ActivitySources it has been told to listen to (AddSource, or an instrumentation's Add...Instrumentation call, which adds its source); a library whose source is not added creates no recorded spans.
claims.source_hint: OpenTelemetry .NET docs 'Getting started' / TracerProviderBuilder.AddSource; .NET docs ActivitySource/ActivityListener (StartActivity returns null without a listener)

claims.text: ASP.NET Core starts an Activity for each request, Npgsql (the library EF Core's PostgreSQL provider uses to send SQL) one per SQL command, HttpClient one per outgoing call; the ASP.NET Core, HttpClient and Npgsql instrumentation make the SDK record them, with no controller change.
claims.source_hint: OpenTelemetry .NET 'Getting started with ASP.NET Core' (source Microsoft.AspNetCore); Npgsql docs 'Diagnostics > Tracing' (AddNpgsql); Npgsql EF Core provider docs

claims.text: With AddOtlpExporter, finished spans are queued and exported in batches by a batch export processor on a background thread (the default export processor type is Batch), so the request is not waiting while spans are sent.
claims.source_hint: OpenTelemetry.Exporter.OpenTelemetryProtocol README (ExportProcessorType default Batch, BatchExportProcessorOptions); OpenTelemetry .NET BatchActivityExportProcessor

claims.text: If the OTLP receiver cannot be reached, spans can be lost but the request is neither delayed nor failed; at stage-3 a service run without the monitoring profile (no Alloy) works the same.
claims.source_hint: OpenTelemetry .NET exporter README (export failures do not throw to the caller); examples/don-hang @ stage-3 docker-compose.yml lines 181-186

claims.text: At stage-3 every service exports spans only to Alloy, which forwards them to Tempo; the services' code never names Tempo, so moving traces to another store changes Alloy's configuration (the otelcol.exporter.otlp block), not the services.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: deploy/monitoring/alloy/config.alloy lines 51-79; docker-compose.yml lines 545-547; STAGE.md diagram

claims.text: builder.Services.AddOpenTelemetry().ConfigureResource(r => r.AddService(name)).WithTracing(t => t.AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation().AddHttpClientInstrumentation().AddSource(...).AddOtlpExporter()) is the syntax used; AddService sets the resource's service.name, the service producing the spans.
claims.source_hint: OpenTelemetry.Extensions.Hosting README; OpenTelemetry .NET docs 'Resources' (AddService sets service.name); examples/don-hang @ stage-3 DonHang.Api/Program.cs lines 107-116

claims.text: The api's AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation Filter leaves out requests to /health and /metrics; AddSource(MessageTracing.SourceName) adds Đơn Hàng's own source 'DonHang.Messaging', defined in DonHang.Messaging/MessageTracing.cs.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: DonHang.Api/Program.cs lines 111-115; DonHang.Messaging/MessageTracing.cs line 16

claims.text: DonHang.Payments and DonHang.Notifications set up tracing in their own Program.cs under the names donhang-payments and donhang-notifications; Notifications, which nothing calls over HTTP, records only its SQL and message spans.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: DonHang.Payments/Program.cs line 67; DonHang.Notifications/Program.cs line 38

claims.text: AddOtlpExporter() with no options reads its endpoint from the environment variable OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT; docker-compose.yml sets it to http://alloy:4317 for each service.
claims.source_hint: OpenTelemetry.Exporter.OpenTelemetryProtocol README 'Environment variables' (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT); examples/don-hang @ stage-3 docker-compose.yml lines 186, 324, 385, 415

claims.text: Alloy's otelcol.receiver.otlp listens for OTLP on port 4317 and passes spans to otelcol.processor.batch, which batches what all services send and via its output passes it to otelcol.exporter.otlp (endpoint tempo:4317); tls insecure = true disables TLS to Tempo.
claims.source_hint: Grafana Alloy docs components otelcol.receiver.otlp, otelcol.processor.batch, otelcol.exporter.otlp; examples/don-hang @ stage-3 deploy/monitoring/alloy/config.alloy lines 54-79

claims.text: The comment starting '// lesson: backend.l3.trace-sampling', the sampleRatio line and SetSampler of DonHang.Api/Program.cs (lines 101-110) decide which traces are kept; that topic belongs to a later lesson.
At stage-3 docker-compose.yml has no OpenTelemetry container; spans are received by Alloy and stored by Tempo, both in the monitoring profile.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: docker-compose.yml lines 181-186, 545-576; STAGE.md profiles table

claims.text: Metrics are scraped by Prometheus from /metrics (pull), while spans are pushed by each service over OTLP.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: DonHang.Api/Program.cs line 100 comment (metrics stay with prometheus-net); Prometheus docs 'Overview' (pull model); OTLP specification (exporter sends to receiver)

claims.text: Try it: with the monitoring profile up, docker compose stop alloy, then curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:8080/api/v1/products prints 200 without waiting for Alloy; docker compose start alloy restores it.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: docker-compose.yml lines 40-45 (port 8080), 181-186; DonHang.Api/Controllers/ProductsController.cs line 23 (anonymous GET)
